title: Contribution of Recycled Moisture to Precipitation in an Inland River Basin Over Temperate Grasslands: Considering Cold‐Warm Air Mass Convergences
content:
Abstract

Vegetation-air mass interactions play a critical role in regulating recycled moisture dynamics in temperate grasslands. This study focused on a representative inland river basin, primarily including typical, meadow, and sparse wood grasslands. To account for the impacts of cold and warm air mass convergence, we improved the isotope-based estimation framework by incorporating the tracer signals from multiple advected vapor sources, identified using a trajectory model. The results indicate that the contribution of recycled moisture to precipitation was suppressed under cold-cold air mass convergence, but enhanced under cold-warm air mass convergence; meadow grasslands showed the largest contribution of recycled moisture to precipitation (43.1%), followed by sparse wood grasslands (41.3%) and typical grasslands (17.6%). The contribution of plant transpiration to precipitation (f tr) was significantly greater than that of surface evaporation (f ev). Specifically, the f tr in meadow grasslands was estimated at 38%, much larger than those in sparse wood grasslands (25.3%) and typical grasslands (9.2%). This highlights that under cold-warm air mass convergence, the intense plant transpiration in meadow grasslands plays a crucial role in regional precipitation formation. The results are important for evaluating the water balance of inland grassland ecosystems.
